To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the boundary terms in the Dirac action for Kerr/CFT are determined by the Dirac equations and that the correlators of spinor fields in a conformal field theory in 2+1 dimensions can be calculated by considering the Dirac equations for spinors in Kerr/CFT.

the requirement that the Dirac action for spinor fields be stationary for solutions with fixed boundary conditions, determines the form of a boundary term that is to be added to this action, and that the two-point function of spinors in Kerr/CFT, as computed with the aid of this boundary term, agrees with the correlators of a two-dimensional relativistic conformal theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the Dirac equation in the Kerr spacetime.
the study of the boundary term of the Dirac action in the context of Kerr/CFT and its consequences for the two-point function of spinor fields.

the study of the Kerr black hole in the framework of Kerr/CFT, a conjectured holographic correspondence between the four dimensional asymptotically flat Kerr black hole and a two dimensional conformal field theory living on the black hole horizon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Kerr/CFT conjecture is true, but it is a bit too early to say that it is proven.
the Kerr/CFT correspondence is not a valid conjecture.
there is a correspondence between a two-dimensional conformal field theory and the boundary of the near-horizon Kerr geometry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in Kerr/CFT, the boundary term for spinors is determined by the requirement that the Dirac equation is satisfied on the boundary and this boundary term leads to the two point function for spinor field in Kerr/CFT being equal to that of a two dimensional CFT.
, the Dirac operator in Kerr/CFT can be written in terms of the Dirac operator on a two dimensional sphere.
, in Kerr/CFT, the boundary term for the Dirac action plays the role of a source for spinor fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the boundary term is not just a mathematical artifact, but is crucial for the consistency of the theory.
the requirement that the Dirac action be stationary for solutions with fixed boundary conditions fixes uniquely the boundary term that must be added to it.
the boundary term for spinor fields is not just a technicality but rather a crucial ingredient for the correct calculation of the correlators.
